title: Teleseismic case identification results of the DiTing 0.1b phase-picking model
abstract: Phase-picking models are usually trained on regional waveforms, and their performance on teleseismic records requires further examination using real data. This study takes the DiTing 0.1b phase-picking model of the DiTing seismic large-model series as the study object and carries out a case-based test of teleseismic phase identification within the DTFlowPro framework, using 15 global earthquakes of M5.0～5.9 that occurred from 22 to 31 December 2024. Two detection branches, the native-sampling branch and a 20 Hz resampling branch, were built. The candidates were fused by taking the union of time-clustered picks. The two branches showed clear complementarity. For P phases, 286 stations produced detections in both branches, 179 only in the native-sampling branch, and 40 only in the 20 Hz branch. The corresponding numbers for the S phase were 29, 19, and 25. The fused detections exactly matched the union of the two branches, and the station detection rates increased to 12.03% for the P phase and 1.74% for the S phase, 0.94 and 0.45 percentage points higher than those of the best single branch. The fused P detection rate decreased from 74.19% at 0°～10° to 4.19% at 90°～100°, and the fused S detection rate decreased from 58.06% at 0°～10° to below 8% beyond 10°. Among the combinations of three association methods and three fixed-depth location objective functions, the combination of native sampling, robust residual iteration, and the weighted L2 norm produced the smallest median epicentral error of 23.66 km. The event-building program dtevent of DTFlowPro merged 1102 phase picks and 359 origin solutions into 15 earthquakes, with no missing, incorrectly merged, or incorrectly split catalog events. This case-based evaluation of 15 typical teleseismic earthquakes indicates that, under catalog-guided conditions, the DiTing 0.1b model provides usable identification of teleseismic P phases within 90°, while the identification of S phases and of P phases beyond 90° remains limited. Because these conclusions are based on a limited number of cases, they should not be extrapolated to an assessment of teleseismic monitoring capability.

title: Towards Hijacking Interactions in Virtual Reality
abstract: We identify and study a new Virtual Reality Interaction Manipulation (VRIM) attack, where a remote attacker takes control of a user's interaction with the VR system, by trapping the user inside a malicious app that masquerades as the full VR interface. Once trapped, the user's interactions with apps, services, and other users can be recorded and modified without their knowledge. We build a prototype of VRIM on Meta Quest headsets and conduct an IRB-approved user study to validate its feasibility and efficacy. We disclosed VRIM and potential defenses to Meta, who responded positively. Our work emphasizes the need for new security measures tailored to the unique immersive nature of VR systems.

title: When and how anthropomorphic AI avatars relate to user engagement intentions: roles of emotional connection, perceived authenticity and technological familiarity
abstract: Purpose This study examines when and how anthropomorphic AI service avatars shape user engagement intentions in digital commerce. Drawing primarily on computers are social actors (CASA) theory and using parasocial interaction (PSI) as a bounded interpretive lens, it examines emotional connection as an encounter-specific affective mechanism and perceived authenticity and technological familiarity as theoretically focal contingencies operating at different stages of the engagement process. Design/methodology/approach Study 1 employed a between-subjects experiment that manipulated higher versus lower levels of bundled visual-form anthropomorphism. Study 2 used a three-wave survey of online shoppers to re-examine the focal relationships in prior AI-avatar service encounters. Mediation, moderation, and conditional indirect associations were estimated using PROCESS with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Findings Study 1 shows that higher visual-form anthropomorphism increases user engagement intention, with emotional connection accounting for a meaningful but partial share of the effect. Study 2 provides associative support for the core relationships, although the association between anthropomorphism and emotional connection is comparatively modest. Perceived authenticity strengthens the theoretically focal association between anthropomorphism and emotional connection, while technological familiarity strengthens the association between emotional connection and engagement intention. The findings indicate that emotional connection represents one mechanism among multiple affective, cognitive and evaluative pathways linking anthropomorphic AI avatars with engagement intentions. Originality/value This study advances interactive marketing research by identifying emotional connection as a meaningful but partial encounter-level mechanism linking AI-avatar anthropomorphism with engagement intentions. It further demonstrates that perceived authenticity and technological familiarity condition the theoretically focal stages of this process, while the dominant direct component highlights the need for a multiple-pathway, rather than exclusively affective, account of AI-avatar engagement.

title: Spontaneity and authorship: a Kantian account of human authorship in copyright law
abstract: Generative AI has revived a neglected question in copyright law: why must authors be human? Courts and copyright offices have largely answered through statutory interpretation, but the underlying jurisprudence remains underdeveloped. This article draws on Kant’s theory of publication and spontaneity to argue that copyright protects an imputable communicative act. A copyright work transcends its status as a produced object to exist fundamentally as a public address attributable to a rational subject capable of authorising its communication. The article grounds this account in the architecture of Kant’s Doctrine of Right: the mandate that authorises publication is a relation between persons, modelled on the Roman mandatum, and the standing from which it issues is an exercise of the author’s innate right of communicative freedom. Current AI systems possess the capacity to generate outputs, yet they remain incapable of originating communicative acts or issuing mandates in the Kantian sense. The article further develops a Mandate Test for human-AI collaboration and concludes that the human authorship requirement follows from the nature of authorship itself, not merely from historical practice or legislative convention.

title: Ultra-short-term PV power prediction based on a dual-stream CNN-GRU-attention framework
abstract: Aiming at the challenges of data noise and cumulative error in photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting, this paper proposes a dat a and model dual-closed-loop ultra-short-term forecasting framework. At the data end, the interquartile range (IQR) method and forward-backward interpolation are utilized to reconstruct outliers, while the Spearman coefficient and sine-cosine encoding are combined to optimize meteorological and temporal features. At the model end, a dual-stream network is constructed using a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) strategy. The historical stream extracts multi-scale temporal features using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) - Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) - Attention mechanism, whereas the future stream resolves weather trends using a GRU. Simulation results show that the model's coefficient of determination reaches 0.983, and simulation comparisons with other models and ablation studies have demonstrated the superiority of the proposed model and the effectiveness of its core components.

title: A Composable AI-Accelerated Iterative Solver for 3D-IC Thermal Modeling
abstract: Accurate thermal analysis of heterogeneous 2.5D/3D-IC packages is essential yet computationally prohibitive. A single full-package FEM simulation can take hours, while AI-based surrogates treat the entire stack as a monolithic prediction target and must be retrained whenever the die count or topology changes. To address this limitation, this work proposes Domain-Decomposed AI-Accelerated Iterative Solver for Thermal Analysis (DAIST), a composable thermal solver that decomposes the global package simulation into block-level subdomain problems, replaces subdomain solvers with neural operators, and couples them through iterative exchanges of interfacial temperature and heat flux. This local-to-global architecture eliminates the topology lock-in of monolithic models: block-level neural operators can be directly reused in unseen package assemblies without retraining. The iterative coupling strategy further provides a controllable accuracy-runtime tradeoff, where the iteration budget can be adjusted to trade accuracy for runtime. Evaluated on a multi-chiplet system and an advanced packaging system, DAIST achieves up to $178\times$ speedup over traditional FEM solvers with mean temperature errors of 0.068% and 0.323%, respectively, while demonstrating cross-topology reuse of block-level models across structurally distinct package assemblies.

title: Watch, Infer, Coordinate: Inferring Robot Partner Constraints for Zero-Shot Coordination
abstract: Robots operating in the physical world will increasingly need to coordinate with other robots, particularly in manipulation tasks where an object may be too large or heavy for a single robot to carry alone. Physical limitations caused by hardware degradation or actuator faults can restrict the actions a robot can reliably execute, yet these limitations may be unknown to its partner. We study whether a helper can infer a robot partner's physical constraints from observing it coordinate with another robot, then use the inferred capability to coordinate with the same partner on a new task. This is difficult because a demonstration shows what the constrained robot did, but not what it could have done. In physically coupled tasks, the other robot may also compensate for its limitations, making those limitations difficult to identify from the constrained robot's behavior alone. Our key insight is that these constraints shape the joint behavior of the team, making the actions of both robots informative about the constrained partner's capability. We introduce Watch, Infer, Coordinate, a benchmark spanning three physically coupled manipulation settings, together with an inference approach that scores candidate constraints using observed joint behavior. Across all three settings, our method substantially improves constraint inference and zero-shot coordination, approaching an oracle with access to the true constraints.

title: Towards a Cloud Fog Edge System for Smart Building
abstract: In this article, we present our vision and recent advancements toward creating a decentralized system capable of learning from real-time data within buildings to support sustainable and privacy-preserving smart environments. Our approach promotes the concept of the building itself as the data center, aligning with the principles of edge computing to safeguard confidentiality and reduce reliance on external cloud infrastructure. This is particularly valuable in humanitarian contexts, where data sovereignty, energy efficiency, and infrastructure constraints are critical. We detail a lightweight, "Kubernetes-like" orchestration framework for deploying AI services within such environments and demonstrate our progress in implementing AI algorithms on low-power, cost-effective microcontrollers such as those in the Arduino ecosystem. By enabling in-situ learning directly on sensors or microcontrollers, our work aims to bring intelligent services to resource-limited settings, fostering autonomy, resilience, and sustainable development in vulnerable or underserved communities. The contributions in this article are related, firstly, to our project "Online Machine Learning Algorithms for Embedded Systems" and the evaluation of two new online algorithms. Secondly, we envision a cloud-fog-edge architecture based on the KOptim and FIWARE components, and we propose a methodology for coupling them. Experimental results of the online algorithms are also presented, showcasing real-world traces.

title: Localisation-Aware Uncertainty for Pretrained Object Detection
abstract: Reliable uncertainty estimation is essential for deploying object detectors when distribution/covariate shift and adversarial attacks may occur. Existing approaches often require detector retraining, architectural modification, or repeated inference, which may be infeasible or incur significant overheads. We introduce a lightweight post-hoc evidential meta-model that learns when object localisations should be considered uncertain while keeping the base detector frozen. Our approach automatically identifies localisation-relevant features and uses saliency-guided modification to construct an increasingly challenging curriculum. Detection-level targets combine localisation error, modification level, and prediction instability to guide an evidential meta-model to estimate uncertainty for each predicted bounding box. Our approach requires no changes to the detector and preserves its original localisation outputs. Across adversarial attacks and evaluated strengths, GRACE improves TP-FP AUROC by 22% relative to the strongest comparator in some cases while maintaining in-distribution detection performance.

title: A Quantum Phase Neural Network with Multi-Inputs/Single-Output
abstract: A 35 input/single output quantum phase neural network (QPNN) is proposed to recognize the English letters' A 'and' B 'composed 7*5 of pixels. Each node of the proposed QPNN has the input with 0 or 1. Through normalization and quantum phase encoding, each set of 35 with 0 or 1 digital inputs is encoded into a quantum superposition state described by 35 quantum phases. Then, a quantum rotation gate is used to introduce adjustable phase, and a controlled NOT gate is used to entangle the relative phase between the two inputs. The relationship between the input and output of the network is derived. This paper also derived the phase weight learning training algorithm with adaptive learning rate. The solutions with the recognition probability of 1 is designed, and the analytical expressions for all adjustable phase solutions with zero errors are not unique. The experimental performance is verified on the Qiskit platform. This paper uses phase drive to convert the probability calculation into an analytical polynomial function with adjustable rotation angles in the network, avoiding the bottleneck of generating all 2^35 complex exponential amplitudes and providing an effective way to solve the "exponential wall" problem, which provides a new implementation solution for the practical application of multi-input recognition problems.

The relationship between the input and output of the network is derived. This paper also derived the phase weight learning training algorithm with adaptive learning rate. The solutions with the recognition probability of 1 is designed, and the analytical expressions for all adjustable phase solutions with zero errors are not unique. The experimental performance is verified on the Qiskit platform. This paper uses phase drive to convert the probability calculation into an analytical polynomial function with adjustable rotation angles in the network, avoiding the bottleneck of generating all 2^35 complex exponential amplitudes and providing an effective way to solve the "exponential wall" problem, which provides a new implementation solution for the practical application of multi-input recognition problems.

title: Lifting the maximally-entangledness assumption in robust self-testing for synchronous games
abstract: Robust self-testing in non-local games allows a classical referee to certify that two untrustworthy players are able to perform a specific quantum strategy up to high precision. Proving robust self-testing results becomes significantly easier when one restricts the allowed strategies to symmetric projective maximally entangled (PME) strategies, which allow natural descriptions in terms of tracial von Neumann algebras. This has been exploited in the celebrated M I P ∗ = R E paper and related articles to prove robust self-testing results for synchronous games when restricting to PME strategies. However, the PME assumptions are not physical, so these results need to be upgraded to make them physically relevant. In this work, we do just that: we prove that any perfect synchronous game which is a robust self-test when restricted to PME strategies, is in fact a robust self-test for all strategies. We then apply our result to the Quantum Low Degree Test to find an efficient n -qubit test.

title: Construction of a Teaching Quality Monitoring and Evaluation System Based on Data Mining Analysis
abstract: In our country, the teacher team construction and management level are constantly improving. It is crucial to enhance education quality, particularly classroom teaching quality. This study explores the application of data mining techniques in teaching quality evaluation. Using a dataset comprising evaluation scores from 10 teachers at a university, we construct a prototype system to demonstrate the proposed methodology, this paper studied the large data mining technology and clustering analysis algorithm, and based on this algorithm, put forward the teaching quality control and evaluation system, and choose a college teacher to students train the system, finally, the application of this system, the application effect is good. The specific conclusions are as follows: (1) compared with Apriori algorithm, FP-growth algorithm and HBE-Apriori algorithm, this algorithm has obvious advantages in operation speed. (2) The theoretical basis of K-mean clustering and the method of evaluating K-mean clustering are given, specific procedures and implementation procedures are given, and finally an example is given to illustrate its process and operation process. There are many ways of evaluation, with an emphasis on analyzing the values of purity and F1. (3) expounds three levels of the platform: performance level, service level and data level. Then, the specific implementation schemes of system initialization design, data collection, data preprocessing and data mining are expounded. (4) There is a close connection between teachers ’education quality and students’ education quality. The corresponding “satisfaction” of “excellent” teachers is 0.8; the education quality of teachers is “good”; if the teaching content is good and the level evaluation confidence is 0.7, the confidence level is 0.5 regardless of whether the level evaluation is satisfactory or basically satisfied, significantly lower than both “good” and “level evaluation”. Another important element is the reasonable arrangement and optimization of the course content. This study employed evaluation scores from ten faculty members at a university as a preliminary pilot dataset to demonstrate the proposed methodological workflow, thereby constructing a prototype system. We explicitly acknowledge that this sample size constitutes the primary limitation of the study, and the generalizability of the conclusions requires further validation. When teaching content is rated as ’excellent,’ the confidence level for a ’satisfactory’ evaluation grade is 0.7; when teaching content is rated as ’good,’ the confidence level for both ’satisfactory’ and ’basically satisfied’ evaluations is 0.5—significantly lower than the level for ’excellent’ teaching content.

title: A comparative study of GCN and GraphSAGE algorithms for structural anomaly detection in public procurement networks
abstract: Bid rigging and procurement collusion may produce structural patterns in the relationships between companies and procurement opportunities. This study compares Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) and GraphSAGE for structural anomaly detection in a heterogeneous company–tender procurement network. The study uses Government Procurement via GeBIZ data from Singapore and introduces controlled synthetic anomalies because the dataset does not provide complete bidder-participation information or verified collusion labels. A leakage-aware temporal evaluation is applied together with multiple anomaly difficulties, random seeds, unseen anomaly subjects, and cross-pattern testing. The results show different empirical behavior between the two architectures. GraphSAGE achieves higher F1-Score, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC in the multi-seed evaluation, while GCN achieves higher recall. GraphSAGE also performs better in the true inductive evaluation on unseen anomaly subjects. An Early Warning System based on GraphSAGE is further developed to rank companies according to their structural anomaly scores. The findings indicate that graph-based models can support structural anomaly screening, while synthetic anomaly results should not be interpreted as evidence of confirmed procurement collusion.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Beginner's Guide
abstract: Artificial Intelligence: A Beginner's Guide provides an accessible introduction to the fundamental concepts, technologies, and applications of Artificial Intelligence. The book explains essential topics such as intelligent systems, machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, and Generative AI in a clear and easy-to-understand manner. It introduces readers to how AI systems learn from data, recognize patterns, make predictions, and support decision-making across diverse domains. The book also explores practical applications of AI in healthcare, education, finance, business, transportation, and everyday technology while addressing important considerations related to ethics, privacy, security, and responsible AI. Designed for beginners, students, educators, and aspiring professionals, the book provides a strong foundation for exploring the rapidly evolving world of Artificial Intelligence.

title: Unmanned Underwater Vehicle Path Following Based on Improved Soft ActorCritic with Action Smoothing
abstract: The deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method shows great potential in unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) motion control. Traditional control methods rely on an accurate UUV model. However, due to the nonlinearity of the UUV model and the complex underwater environment, it is difficult to obtain an accurate model in practice. Therefore, we propose a DRL-based path-following control method for UUV. Specifically, this method integrates the Soft Actor–Critic (SAC), prioritized experience replay (PER), and policy smoothing methods to improve the generalization, tracking accuracy, and smoothness of the controller. PER assigns greater sampling weights to samples with high learning efficiency. Another major challenge in the UUV control problem arises from the action oscillations induced by the DRL policy. This problem leads to excessive wear of the actuator system and difficulty in practical applications. To address this, an improved policy regularization method is designed to promote action smoothness. In addition, a dynamic reward function that integrates tracking error, motion state, and control signals is designed to improve training efficiency. The simulation results show that improved SAC has a smooth control signal and good tracking accuracy in different waypoint configurations and uncertain disturbances.

title: Programming with Composable Recursive Patterns and Transformations
abstract: Data processing using traditional pattern matching syntax and direct recursive functions is straightforward to write but becomes awkward in ambiguous (i.e., nondeterministic) cases: when programmers wish to avoid backtracking, they often end up having to write complicated code that sacrifices clarity and modularity. However, when the tree language being matched is regular, better solutions are possible. This paper presents composable recursive patterns and transformations (CRPTs), a new programming language feature designed to tackle this problem. CRPTs resemble and act like recursive type definitions in a structurally-typed language, which can be composed seamlessly to type check programs, but they also have a runtime component: they are compiled into backtracking-free code that recognizes and transforms their input in linear time. They serve both to validate existing data—for example, when checking structured JSON input against a CRPT that acts as a data schema—and to transform data in a type-safe and efficient manner. We formalize the dynamic semantics of CRPTs, a static type system for them, and a translation into efficient code that executes in time linear in the size of the input and polynomial in the size of the pattern. We also demonstrate the practicality of CRPTs with an implementation in the MLscript programming language, which we evaluate against comparable existing approaches on several examples.

title: Refined² Environment Classifiers
abstract: MetaML-style multi-stage programming (MSP) supports quasi-quotation-based code generation, runtime execution of generated code, and cross-stage persistence (CSP). However, its interaction with computational effects is subtle: mutable state can cause scope extrusion, where generated code escapes the scope of variables on which it depends. This paper presents a type system for MetaML-style MSP with mutable state that statically rules out harmful scope extrusion while supporting multi-level code generation, runtime execution, and a variant of CSP. Our system builds on refined environment classifiers (RECs), a discipline that annotates code types with the variable scopes on which generated code depends. To scale RECs to the MetaML-style setting, we refine classifiers so that they track not only variable scopes, but also the scopes of classifiers themselves. Further, we integrated polymorphism over classifiers, enabling more general and reusable code generation patterns in a multi-level setting. For the resulting system, we define an operational semantics via a definitional interpreter and prove type soundness and safety of offline code generation, showing that generated code can be extracted as standalone well-typed programs. We provide working implementations and mechanized proofs in Rocq.

title: VFedHeal: heterogeneity-aware vertical federated learning with dynamic privacy scheduling for personalized healthcare sensing
abstract: Abstract Vertical federated learning (VFL) can combine aligned medical and wearable data without pooling raw features, but fixed synchronization wastes communication under device heterogeneity, repeated exchanges expose private information, and population models transfer poorly across individuals. We propose VFedHeal, a personalized healthcare VFL system that integrates delay-aware FedBCD, dynamic budget scheduling differential privacy (DBS-DP), and chronological subject calibration. The scheduler assigns faster parties more local updates and sets synchronization intervals from measured processing times. DBS-DP clips exchanged representations and adds Gaussian noise on a public schedule; its fixed zero-concentrated differential privacy budget yields an explicit privacy bound for each party. For a new participant, VFedHeal retains encoders learned from other participants and adjusts only three class-bias parameters using a small set of early labeled trials. Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and NUS-WIDE assess convergence and inference resistance; AFFEC and WESAD test multimodal physiological sensing. On AFFEC, subject-calibrated VFL achieved a macro- F 1 of 0.478, compared with 0.475 for centralized fusion. End-to-end VFedHeal achieved a macro- F 1 of 0.471 with 47.5% less communication than personalized vanilla VFL. The scheduler reduced communication by 51.9% on WESAD. The proposed framework supports personalized healthcare VFL with adaptive coordination and privacy schedules calibrated to the target cohort and sensing modalities.

title: Automatic classification of participants’ role in cyberbullying
abstract: Cyberbullying is the evolution of bullying over an electronic medium. Most existing studies focus on detecting cyberbullying by analyzing the textual content of interactions. Yet, the interaction between participants in cyberbullying conversations was poorly understood as most studies disregard content from victims and bystanders and focus on the bully. This study aimed to develop and evaluate model for identifying cyberbullying participants' roles, including harassers, victims, and bystander defenders, thus broadening the scope to encompass all interaction roles. Conventional Machine Learning (CML) and Transfer Learning (TL) methods were employed on the AMiCA English dataset, which encompasses a broad spectrum of cyberbullying scenarios and detailed role annotations. We conducted a comparative analysis of different techniques to select the most effective model. A comparative analysis of various techniques was performed to identify the most effective model. CML approach incorporated various feature sets includes textual, embedding, sentiment and emotional, psycholinguistics and toxicity features, as well as term lists. With newly integrated toxicity and brand-new psycholinguistics features, Linguistic Inquiry and Word (LIWC) 2022 and Empath, this study set a new benchmark for role identification. Contextual embeddings from ggeluBert, tnBert, and DistilBert achieved noteworthy results, with DistilBert emerging as the most effective across role classes. Feature engineering revealed that textual features and DistilBert embeddings, both independently and in combination, offered the most predictive power. The overall CML models effectiveness was improved when provided with diverse feature combinations, with Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) outperformed Linear Support Vector Classifier (SVC). TL approaches using fine-tuned Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) like DistilBert, DistilRoBerta, and Electra-small outperformed CML models, with optimized DistilBert yielding the highest macro F-measure of 70.6% achieving about 10 percentage points (p.p) increase in performance compared to existing benchmarks and improved recall score across all role classes. This improvement underscores the state-of-the-art PLMs to more effectively identify and differentiate the nuanced roles of participants in cyberbullying scenarios. Additionally, a Streamlit application was developed to detect and classify the roles of participants. However, the models in this study currently classify only English text, limiting their broader linguistic applicability. Future work could explore new directions, including sarcasm detection to address contextual overlaps in harasser and victim messages, expanding the framework to capture interactional dynamics between posts, and adapting it for multilingual and multimodal data.

title: Multi‐Strategy Snow Ablation Optimizer for Global Optimization
abstract: ABSTRACT The snow ablation optimizer (SAO) is a novel meta‐heuristic algorithm inspired by the natural processes of snow melting and sublimation. SAO employs a dual‐population dynamic adjustment mechanism to balance exploration and exploitation, demonstrating significant performance in global optimization. However, when dealing with complex optimization problems, the SAO algorithm tends to suffer from low convergence accuracy and premature convergence. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multi‐strategy snow ablation optimizer (MSSAO). Firstly, it adopts an external archive mechanism to prevent convergence to local optima. Secondly, it utilizes an adaptive t ‐distribution perturbation strategy to achieve a balance between exploration and exploitation. Finally, it employs a mirror reflection learning strategy to maintain population diversity. Comprehensive experiments conducted on the CEC2017 and CEC2022 test suites demonstrate that MSSAO significantly enhances both global optimization performance and convergence accuracy. Furthermore, its effectiveness in engineering optimization is demonstrated through a DC motor control system.

title: Sparse Hamiltonian simulation with optimal dependence on the maximum column Euclidean norm
abstract: We give a quantum algorithm for simulating a $d$-sparse Hermitian Hamiltonian $H$, assuming a known upper bound $Λ$ on its maximum column Euclidean norm $\|H\|_{1\to2}$. For $tΛ\ge1/2$, simulation with operator-norm error $ε$ uses \[ O\!\left(tΛ\sqrt d+\sqrt d\log(2/ε)\right) \] sparse-oracle queries. This removes the subpolynomial overhead in Low's algorithm [STOC 2019], replacing it with an additive logarithmic precision term. For $d>1$ and $tΛ\ge\log(2/ε)$, the bound matches the worst-case lower bound. A known spectral-norm upper bound may also be used in place of $Λ$. The number of 1- and 2-qubit gates is linear in the query scale, up to oracle costs and polynomial overhead in the input bit lengths and logarithmic precision parameters. As applications, we obtain $O(κ\sqrt d\,\mathrm{polylog}(κ/ε))$ queries for solving $d$-sparse quantum linear systems with $\|A\|\le1$ and $\|A^{-1}\|\leκ$, under standard sparse and state-preparation access. We also give a gate-efficient implementation of black-box unitaries with at most $d$ nonzero entries per row and column using $O(\sqrt d\log(2/ε))$ queries, given sparse access to the unitary and its adjoint. At constant error, the query bound is optimal and yields $Θ(\sqrt N)$ queries for arbitrary $N\times N$ unitaries, resolving the open question on black-box unitary implementation posed by Berry and Childs [QIC 2012].

title: Non-Markovian effects on informational steady states
abstract: Informational steady states (ISSs) arise when the rate at which information is gained from continuous measurements is exactly balanced by the rate at which information from earlier measurements is lost to the environment. While ISSs have been studied in Markovian settings, relatively little is known about how memory effects influence their formation and steady-state properties. In this work, we investigate non-Markovian effects on ISSs within the framework of continuously monitored collision models. title: Smoother Flow Matching via Contrastive Trajectory Repulsion
abstract: Trajectory crossing remains a critical bottleneck in Flow Matching (FM), and previous works typically view these crossings from a theoretical optimization perspective causing velocity averaging. They attempt to address it indirectly by post-hoc distillation or endpoint coupling, without explicitly regulating the intermediate trajectories. In this paper, we introduce a new network learning perspective: crossing points inherently induce large local Lipschitz constants in the target velocity field, leading to two drawbacks. First, high Lipschitz constants correspond to high-frequency signals in the velocity field that neural networks struggle to fit due to spectral bias. Second, they also imply drastic velocity variations, leading to severe numerical integration errors in few-step inference. To alleviate this, we propose CoFlow, a framework that introduces the contrastive learning paradigm into FM to explicitly repel trajectories during training, thereby lowering the local Lipschitz constants of the velocity field. Specifically, we formulate CoFlow from a Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) perspective by injecting a repulsive drift term. This drift actively guides the forward process of positive samples away from negative trajectories, effectively reducing the local Lipschitz constant. Furthermore, we derive an equivalent stochastic interpolant formulation from this SDE, providing a simple and tractable design space to control the influence of negative samples. Extensive experiments on ImageNet 256x256 demonstrate that CoFlow significantly reduces FID compared to standard FM in few-step inference (e.g., 20 steps), with no added training overhead. The code can be accessed at: https://github.com/HKUST-LongGroup/CoFlow

title: RelationVGGT: Visual Geometry Transformers for 3D Spatial Relation Segmentation
abstract: Recent advances in 3D reconstruction have progressed from per-scene optimization to feed-forward inference, and semantic scene understanding has followed suit -- yet existing methods remain confined to object-centric perception, neglecting spatial relations between objects. We formulate 3D spatial relation segmentation in a feed-forward, pose-free multi-view setting: given a visually specified subject and a relational text query, the model segments the target across views without receiving its category name. To this end, we propose RelationVGGT, a novel feed-forward framework that integrates semantic features from a visual foundation model with geometry-aware representations from a 3D geometry foundation model and leverages a relation transformer for subject-conditioned, cross-view relation prediction -- requiring neither per-scene optimization nor known camera poses. We additionally provide a fully automated annotation pipeline built on ScanNet++ with VLMs and LLMs, enabling scalable training data generation for this new task.

title: Fast Wasserstein rates for estimating probability distributions of probabilistic graphical models
abstract: Using i.i.d. data to estimate a high-dimensional distribution in Wasserstein distance is a fundamental instance of the curse of dimensionality. We explore how structural knowledge about the data-generating process, which gives rise to the distribution can be used to overcome this curse. More precisely, we work with the set of distributions of probabilistic graphical models for a given directed acyclic graph. It turns out that this knowledge is only helpful if it can be quantified, which we formalize via smoothness conditions on the transition kernels in the disintegration corresponding to the graph. In this case, we prove that the rate of estimation is governed by the local structure of the graph, more precisely by dimensions corresponding to single nodes together with their parent nodes. The precise rate depends on the exact notion of smoothness assumed for the kernels, where either weak (Wasserstein–Lipschitz) or strong (bidirectional total variation Lipschitz) conditions lead to different results. We prove sharpness under the strong condition and show that this condition covers, as a special case, distributions having a positive Lipschitz density.

title: Urheberrechtsverletzung durch Memorisierung und Output von Musikwerken in KI‑Systemen
abstract: Zusammenfassung Gegenstand des Rechtstreits vor dem LG München I war eine Klage der Verwertungsgesellschaft GEMA gegen die Anbieterin eines KI‑Systems wegen Urheberrechtsverletzungen, weil die Anbieterin in ihrem KI‑System Melodien bekannter Künstler wiedergibt, die von der GEMA vertreten werden, ohne mit der GEMA einen Lizenzvertrag abgeschlossen zu haben. Das Gericht erörtert auf 137 Seiten mit 559 Randziffern ausführlich wichtige urheberrechtliche Rechtsfragen im Hinblick auf die Nutzung des KI‑Systems. Die Entscheidung des Gerichts beruht nicht nur auf deutschem bzw. europäischem, sondern auch auf US‑amerikanischem Recht, weil das Gericht sich hierzu aufgrund einer besonderen Zuständigkeitsregelung im Verwertungsgesellschaftengesetz (VGG) berechtigt bzw. verpflichtet sieht.

title: Securing Enterprise Language Model Applications Against Data Leakage and Response Manipulation
abstract: Enterprise language-model applications combine internal documents, retrieval, conversation history, and executable tools. This critical narrative and thematic review examines data leakage and response manipulation through targeted discovery completed on September 29, 2026, with a bounded supplementary discovery and source-status audit on October 1, 2026. Primary studies are distinguished from institutional guidance and contextual reviews. The evidence identifies indirect prompt injection, corpus poisoning, retrieval-stage exploitation, log contamination, embedding inversion, and cumulative knowledge-base extraction under different conditions (Chang et al., 2026; Greshake et al., 2023; Morris et al., 2023; Yao et al., 2026). Defensive studies address provenance signaling, structured training, preference optimization, capability enforcement, and action attribution, with configuration-dependent findings (Chen, Piet, et al., 2025; Chen, Zharmagambetov, et al., 2025; Debenedetti et al., 2026; He et al., 2026). The synthesis proposes six assurance boundaries: identity and scope, source authorization, content provenance, model interaction, executable actions, and output release. Provider and inference-data handling, monitoring, and incident response span all six. Authoritative confidentiality and authorization decisions require application or infrastructure controls independent of unconstrained model interpretation. The framework is an author-developed, unvalidated decision aid, not a certification or a NIST/OWASP-endorsed standard. A hypothetical assistant and prospective protocol illustrate permission-preserving processing, cumulative-disclosure budgets, revocation propagation, legitimate-task utility, and verification effort. No original experiment, complete database census, or universal estimate of compromise is claimed.

title: A Review on Automated Data Curation Pipelines for LargeScale Web Text in Generative AI Pretraining
abstract: The fast development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) models has boosted the need of large-scale datasets of web text of high quality to pre-train. However, raw web data collected by large sources (such as Common Crawl) is usually noisy, repetitive, biased, irrelevant, and of poor text quality, which negatively affect the model performance, training performance, and ethical accuracy. The conceptual framework of automated quality filtering and structuring of large-scale web text data used in this review paper is specifically designed to the generative AI pre-training pipelines. The proposed system combines automated web crawling, data cleaning, deduplication, content filtering, semantic quality estimation and structured dataset generation in one single pipeline. Some of the key aspects of automated data quality evaluation systems, are discussed as data cleaning using machine learning, quality scoring using perplexity, self-distillation, and noisy data processing, and semantic information retrieval. The review also looks at the current data documentation methods like data sheets of datasets, synthetic data generation techniques and retrieval-augmented systems to enhance data reliability and traceability. Furthermore, the issues of scalability, the risk of privacy in training data, and the necessity of using AI in a responsible manner by establishing automated monitoring and filtering systems are also mentioned in the research. The provided framework is likely to improve the quality of the given data set, reduce the noise and repetition, make the training be more efficient, and contribute to building more reliable, accurate, and ethical generative AI models. This review will add to the current body of knowledge as it will synthesize the recent literature in automated data filtering, web data structuring, and scaling AI data pipeline design, and will suggest a holistic approach to automated web text data preparation to generative AI pre-training setups..

title: Covering codes checked by the Lean kernel: K_7(9,4) <= 1134, ten more upper bounds, K_2(6,1) = 12, and K_7(4,2) = 19
abstract: Lean 4 proofs, against Mathlib v4.34.1 and checked by the kernel with no sorry and no native_decide, of upper bounds on the covering number K_q(n,R) for eleven cells, each by an explicit code below the corresponding table entry we found: K_7(9,4) <= 1134 (best published 1475, Marosi, arXiv:2608.19872v3), K_7(10,4) <= 5607 (previously 6517), K_5(11,4) <= 2875 (previously 3125) and K_5(10,5) <= 162 (previously 175), three cells unchanged in Kéri's tables since at least 2004, and K_7(8,3) <= 1887, K_5(10,4) <= 625, K_5(9,3) <= 1250, K_5(7,2) <= 500, K_5(9,4) <= 250, K_4(10,4) <= 192, K_5(9,5) <= 50. Two certificates: digit prefixes (12 CPU-hours for (Z/7)^9) and syndromes of a linear base (minutes; the 5616-word code in 11 minutes on four cores), each new certificate also tested by mutations that the kernel rejects. All codes are cosets of a linear code plus a patch; for K_7(9,4) the base comes from an enumeration of all 6362 classes of non-degenerate [9,3]_7 codes, and the 105-word patch is optimal among patches invariant under translation along either of the two lines of the base solved to optimality by integer programming. A literature search over 2103 works found no smaller published code in the four cells. K_7(4,2) = 19 (previously 17 <= K <= 19), and new in this version the equality is entirely checked by the kernel, with no hypothesis (K742.K_7_4_2_eq_19, K742.K_7_4_2_isK): the upper bound is an explicit code; the non-existence of an 18-word code reduces, by lemmas and a code-to-CNF bridge proved in Lean, to 70 SAT instances whose LRAT refutations are replayed inside the kernel by a verified checker (284 modules, 37.8 CPU-hours); the same refutations were checked by two independent checkers outside Lean and confirmed by a second, independent encoding. Also new: a machine-checked ledger of covering-code upper bounds, with formally certified exact entries. Each of the 1145 cells of Kéri's tables carries a certification state and provenance per bound; 700 of the 1145 upper bounds are theorems of the Lean kernel, almost all in a single theorem, from a generic bound K_q(n,R) <= |C|, construction rules and explicit witnesses. The lower bounds remain citations of the literature, except K_2(6,1) and K_7(4,2), whose exact values are formalized on both sides. Also K_2(6,1) >= 11 by double counting and K_2(6,1) = 12 by a search with a soundness proof. New in version 0.9.0: three exact values that are potentially new (not found in the literature we searched), whose lower bounds are verified computational certificates checked by exact programs outside Lean, not theorems of the kernel. K_3(6,2) = 17 (previously 15 <= K <= 17; Bertolo-Östergård-Weakley 2004, doi:10.1002/jcd.20008, and Hämäläinen-Rankinen 1991, doi:10.1016/0097-3165(91)90024-B): after a normalization by a minimal fibre, codes with 15 or 16 words fall into 12049 and 12674 instances whose linear relaxations are infeasible by 12054 and 13099 integer Farkas certificates checked in exact arithmetic, independently reproduced by a second pipeline with no code in common (VeriPB and LRAT proofs); the upper bound 17 is a kernel theorem in the ledger. K_7(6,4) = 14 (previously 13 <= K <= 15; Haas-Schlage-Puchta-Quistorff 2009, Kéri-Östergård 2005): a new 14-word code, formalized in Lean, and LRAT refutations of the 8008 fibre profiles of a 13-word code, from a fibre lemma for K_q(n,n-2). K_7(5,3) = 17 (previously 15 <= K <= 17, both announced in Kéri's tables): LRAT refutations of one profile for 15 words and of all 201376 profiles for 16 words; the upper bound 17 was the announced one, with no published code. New in version 0.9.1: a 17-word code of our own for K_7(5,3), whose covering property is a theorem of the Lean kernel (CoveringK753.K_7_5_3_le_17, axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only), so both bounds of K_7(5,3) = 17 are now established here, the upper one in the kernel and the lower one as verified computational certificates. Each lower bound survived an adversarial review; the remaining gaps (for example, 9 large LRAT proofs of K_7(5,3) not regenerated by the review, and no Lean proof of the three lower bounds) are stated in the paper, together with the limits of the same methods on other open cells. New in version 0.10.0: K_4(7,4) ≥ 10 and K_4(6,3) ≥ 12 (previously 9 and 11), by LRAT refutations of all 792 and 8008 fibre profiles, from the fibre lemma extended to every radius up to n-2, checked by lrat-check and again by a second solver on every profile and by an independent encoding on a sample; these are verified computational certificates outside Lean, new in the ledger; we did not find them in the sources we read, but novelty is not established (one source, Haas 2011, Ars Combin. 99, not read), and an independent adversarial review is pending. With a 10-word code of our own checked by the official verifier, K_4(7,4) = 10. The certified upper bounds rise to the count stated above (bases outside the batch generator and 26 linear codes found by search), all equal to published values. Negative results recorded: tabu search with and without prescribed groups ties four records and beats none, and construction programs evolved by a language model lost to plain local search. The paper adds the method (witness, independent verifier, kernel, objective bound), the infrastructure with a budget enforced in code, and related work on mathematics with AI in 2026; every ledger count in the paper is generated from the ledger by a script.

title: 思兼 Omoikane Core Ver.8.0.0: Realizable Evidence Architecture
abstract: Abstract We introduce Omoikane Core Ver.8.0.0, a realizable evidence architecture that extends the Omoikane framework from formal evidence sufficiency to acquisition executability. Earlier Omoikane layers address identification, noisy and composite inference, model uncertainty, anytime-valid analysis, adaptive selection, dependent evidence fusion, replication, transport, and replay. Ver.8 adds a distinct realization coordinate, Sigma_8 = (Sigma_7, r), because a formally valid bridge need not be executable by the instrument, specimen, computation, archive, or network expected to provide its observations. We model realization as a stateful acquisition system with admissible controls, observable continuation states, joint outcome/state-transition kernels, and pathwise resource costs. Exact implementation is defined by candidate-independent Blackwell randomization, while approximate implementation is quantified by total-variation protocol deficiency. For finite deterministic systems, exact realized identification holds precisely when the target is constant on every reachable transcript fiber. A destructive two-bit construction gives a strict non-factorization witness: both formal tests are individually realizable, yet no executable sequence realizes the complete bridge because the first measurement destroys the unique specimen. Its minimax protocol deficiency is exactly 1/2, whereas the nondestructive counterpart has deficiency zero. Thus pointwise realizability does not imply sequence realizability, and realization status is not determined by the complete formal Ver.7 certificate. For approximate sequential implementation, continuation-aware one-step debts eta_t yield the bound Delta_T <= 1 - product_t(1 - eta_t) <= sum_t eta_t under the stated measurable-coupling conditions. Formal target risk therefore transfers to realized risk with an additive protocol-deficiency penalty. We further show that outcome-only Blackwell improvement can worsen sequential performance when it damages future acquisition capability. This motivates continuation-preserving Blackwell refinement, which preserves the observable continuation state and its correlation with the report, together with pathwise budget preservation. Candidate-independent simulation or post-processing cannot bootstrap a missing acquisition channel; it can only garble information already acquired. The framework separates formal validity, acquisition realization, referent/model realization, and actual-target truth through a realization lock and an actuality-promotion firewall. It does not claim a new Blackwell order, a universal controlled-sensing algorithm, a universal feasibility solver, or a truth oracle. Its contribution is a typed operational layer connecting comparison of statistical experiments, Le Cam deficiency, sequential experimental design, controlled sensing, reachability, resource-constrained acquisition, and scientific claim promotion. A deterministic verifier independently audits the finite load-bearing examples and numerical bounds.

title: Replication data and code for: Local Earthquake Intensity and Place-Directed Online Attention: A Global Multi-Event Study
abstract: This reproducibility package contains the frozen research protocol, analysis-level earthquake-place data, data provenance manifest, Python source code, automated tests, saved model outputs, validation reports, diagnostics, and source data for the reported figures and tables. It supports inspection and reproduction of the analyses reported in “Local Earthquake Intensity and Place-Directed Online Attention: A Global Multi-Event Study.” The package uses public data derived from USGS, GeoNames, Wikidata/MediaWiki, and Wikimedia Analytics. One external USGS event-detail record remained unavailable after documented retries; this limitation is disclosed, while the included validation suite records 23 of 23 protocol checks passing and 121 automated tests passing. No human-participant records, personal identifiers, IP addresses, usernames, or individual browsing histories are included. Version 1.0.1 aligns the archived secondary-model inference and model-fit fields with the manuscript and supporting table. Point estimates and substantive conclusions are unchanged.

title: Exploring Personality and Creativity in an LLM-Based Serious Game: A First Approach
abstract: This paper presents AbstractMindsAI, a preliminary serious game that explores personality traits and creativity through emotional interaction with abstract art. The system consists of a web-based 3D museum where users engage with artworks through an LLM-based conversational agent that elicits and guides emotional interpretations grounded in visual features. During gameplay, linguistic features extracted from user dialogue are used to estimate personality traits based on the Five-Factor Model (commonly referred to as OCEAN) and creativity dimensions inspired by the Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking. An initial experimental framework is proposed in which users complete standardized assessments before and after repeated interaction. The objective is to explore the feasibility of inferring psychological traits from dialogue and the potential of LLM-guided art interaction to support creativity.

title: PromptWAF: Detecting and Preventing Prompt-Induced Application Vulnerabilities
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly evolve from passive text-generation systems into autonomous agents capable of interacting with external tools, databases, file systems, and operating environments, they introduce new attack surfaces that extend beyond conventional prompt manipulation. In particular, hybrid prompt injection attacks can embed malicious natural-language instructions designed to trigger application-layer vulnerabilities, including path traversal, SQL injection, and command injection. General-purpose prompt injection detectors are often insufficient for identifying such domain-specific, obfuscated, and execution-oriented payloads. To address this limitation, this study introduces PromptWAF, a modular, multi-layer defense orchestrator designed to intercept and neutralize adversarial prompts before they reach the underlying LLM or associated execution pipeline. As a core contribution, we construct and publicly release extensive domain-specific datasets covering LLM-mediated path traversal, SQL injection, and command injection attacks, thereby providing a reusable benchmark for the systematic evaluation of security mechanisms against execution-oriented prompt threats. Using these datasets, several transformer-based architectures, including DistilBERT, RoBERTa, and DeBERTa-v3, are systematically fine-tuned and evaluated. In addition, VulnMCP, a vulnerable testing environment based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), is developed to emulate chained exploit scenarios in agentic LLM applications. Experimental results obtained on an isolated external test set show that the proposed models substantially outperform zero-shot baselines. The final PromptWAF ensemble achieves consistently high detection performance and near-perfect recall across the targeted attack categories, demonstrating its effectiveness in blocking specialized adversarial prompts while maintaining deployment-oriented modularity. To support reproducibility, facilitate independent validation, and accelerate further research on LLM-induced application-layer attacks, we openly release the curated datasets together with the fine-tuned models and the VulnMCP evaluation framework.

title: Asymmetric Discrete-Time Hopfield Neural Networks: Orientation Selectivity
abstract: This paper introduces and formalizes the concept of orientation selectivity in asymmetric discrete-time Hopfield neural networks (ADHNNs). It demonstrates that networks with asymmetric synaptic weight matrices exhibit fundamentally different dynamic behaviors depending on whether the network states are interpreted as row or column vectors, leading to distinct left-side and right-side dynamics. The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of ADHNN dynamics with rank-one asymmetric weight matrices and introduces a novel recording rule based on convex optimization for programming ADHNNs for associative memory tasks. Computational experiments show that ADHNNs programmed with this new method exhibit superior noise tolerance and memory capacity compared with symmetric Hopfield networks with the pseudo-inverse rule, particularly when storing large numbers of patterns. These findings align with recent advances in modern Hopfield networks and dense associative memories, suggesting that weight asymmetry is not only biologically plausible but also computationally advantageous for memory storage and retrieval applications.

title: Dynamic Prediction of Clinical Endpoints in Survival Analysis With Machine and Deep Learning: A Systematic Review and Regulatory Perspective
abstract: Accurate prediction of time-to-event outcomes is essential for clinical decision-making and model-informed drug development (MIDD). Conventional survival models may inadequately represent complex longitudinal patient trajectories, time-dependent treatments, and evolving biomarker or pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) profiles. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have enabled dynamic survival models that update individualized risk predictions as new longitudinal information becomes available. This report systematically reviews dynamic survival modeling frameworks, including extensions of Cox proportional hazards (CPH) with time-varying covariates, discrete-time landmarking strategies, random survival forests (RSF), and deep learning approaches such as DeepHit, Dynamic-DeepHit, and neural ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Applications span sepsis detection, cancer prognosis, and neurodegenerative disease progression. Dynamic models generally achieved discrimination comparable to or better than static Cox models when longitudinal data were available; however, calibration was rarely reported, external validation was uncommon, and integration of PK/PD features into dynamic survival frameworks remains underexplored. Integrating exposure-response modeling with dynamic ML/DL may advance precision dosing, support adaptive trial design, and enhance translational relevance in pharmaceutical research. Emerging regulatory frameworks, including ICH M15 and FDA draft guidance on artificial intelligence in drug development, further emphasize clearly defined contexts of use, risk-based model assessment, credibility, and transparent reporting. Dynamic prediction at the intersection of ML/DL, PK/PD, and regulatory science represents a promising path toward clinically deployable models to inform drug development and regulatory decision-making.

title: Rethinking World-Action Model for Compositional and In-Context Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Long-horizon compositional manipulation has become increasingly important for real-world robot deployment, where a single task involves multiple coordinated subtasks. Existing world-action models (WAMs) jointly predict short-horizon visual futures and actions, but typically lack explicit subtask-level reasoning. We propose Visual Goal-conditioned Action Reasoning (ViGAR), a hierarchical framework that factorizes manipulation into a visual subgoal planner and a subgoal executor. Given the current observation and global instruction, the subgoal planner predicts a visual subgoal for the next subtask. The subgoal executor then jointly generates future visual trajectories and actions conditioned on the predicted subgoal. Both components share a pretrained world-model representation, enabling task-level planning and action generation to benefit from common physical knowledge. Moreover, our framework naturally supports in-context learning: using a global goal image as context can induce different subtask decompositions and behaviors without parameter updates. On the RoboTwin Clean2Random benchmark, ViGAR achieves 82.00% and 67.02% success rates under the Clean and Random settings, respectively, surpassing the strongest baseline by 12.86 percentage points in average success rate. Real-world robot experiments on five compositional and two in-context learning tasks further confirm the effectiveness of ViGAR.

title: Shared-State Local Translations for Training-Free Voice Conversion
abstract: In one-shot training-free voice conversion (VC), the source and reference utterances may contain different linguistic content, so reliable frame-level correspondence between them cannot be assumed. We propose StateVC, which jointly defines a common set of local regions from pooled frame-level WavLM representations of the source and reference utterances; we refer to these regions as states. These shared states are obtained by fitting a pair-specific Gaussian mixture model to the pooled representations, without explicit source--reference frame matching. Within each state, StateVC estimates a source-to-reference mean shift in the original WavLM space. Source-frame posterior probabilities then combine the state-specific shifts so that different frames can receive different local updates. For the LibriSpeech one-shot protocol, StateVC achieves the lowest word error rate (WER) and character error rate (CER) among the evaluated systems, at 8.01% and 3.22%, respectively, with a speaker similarity (SIM) of 0.9512. It also achieves the highest mean perceived speaker similarity among the evaluated systems and the highest mean naturalness among the evaluated training-free systems.

title: Contrastive Attention Mitigates Spectral Bias in Spiking Transformers
abstract: Spiking Transformers merge the energy-efficiency of spiking neural networks (SNNs) with the representational power of self-attention, creating a promising architecture for high-performance, energy-efficient computation. However, a performance gap persists versus its counterparts in artificial neural networks (ANNs). Unlike prior works attributing this to binary activations, we reveal that both spiking neurons and spiking self-attention (SSA) act as low-pass filters through multiscale spectral analysis. This characteristic leads to the dissipation of high-frequency components. To address this issue, we propose the Spiking Contrastive Attention (SCA) paradigm, which draw inspiration from the edge-detection and differential sensing properties of biological visual system. By extracting contrast prototypes via global contrastive aggregation and applying local differential refinement, SCA effectively enhances high-frequency information. Extensive experiments show that SCA is a general module that consistently boosts Spiking Transformers across image classification, semantic segmentation, and event-based tracking. Furthermore, it achieves lower complexity, offering superior efficiency over original SSA. These results establish its potential as a fundamental building block for energy-efficient Spiking Transformers.

title: Granthi: Higher-Order Quantum Programming via Unitary Wiring
abstract: Existing quantum programming languages confine higher-order structure to a classical host while restricting the quantum layer to first-order operations on qubits. This paper presents Granthi, a purely unitary higher-order quantum programming language built on three design commitments: quantum programs are first-class values that may be passed, returned, and coherently composed; additive structure is tag-preserving routing rather than observational branching, so control may remain in superposition; and programmer-facing finite label types with named reversible operations provide domain-level control spaces without exposing tag management. Every well-typed term—including at function type—denotes a unitary on its boundary interface, and the compiler realizes exactly its wiring as a quantum circuit on the physical qubit layout (assuming correctness of the pytket backend). Granthi is implemented end-to-end: an OCaml DSL elaborates surface programs through a binder-free core IR to executable quantum circuits via pytket. The language directly supports the quantum switch—the paper’s running example, compiled to a static circuit—as well as interference on control-flow history and structured finite control, all within the purely unitary fragment.

title: Vector symbolic algebras for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus
abstract: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus for Artificial General Intelligence (ARC-AGI) is a generative, few-shot fluid intelligence benchmark. Although humans effortlessly solve ARC-AGI, it remains extremely difficult for even the most advanced artificial intelligence systems. Inspired by methods for modelling human intelligence spanning neuroscience to psychology, we propose a cognitively inspired ARC-AGI solver. Our solver integrates System 1 intuitions with System 2 reasoning in an efficient and interpretable process using neurosymbolic methods based on Vector Symbolic Algebras (VSAs). Our solver works by object-centric program synthesis, leveraging VSAs to represent abstract objects, guide solution search, and enable sample-efficient neural learning. Preliminary results indicate success, with our solver scoring 10.8% on ARC-AGI-1-Train and 3.0% on ARC-AGI-1-Eval. Additionally, our solver performs well on simpler benchmarks, scoring 94.5% on Sort-of-ARC and 83.1% on 1D-ARC-the latter outperforming GPT-4 at a tiny fraction of the computational cost. Importantly, our approach is unique; we believe we are the first to apply VSAs to ARC-AGI and have developed one of the most cognitively plausible ARC-AGI solvers yet. Our code is available at: https://github.com/ijoffe/ARC-VSA-2025.

title: Mapping the Evolution of Sentiment Analysis in Disaster Management: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: In order to conduct a thorough and transparent bibliometric evaluation of the academic works related to sentiment analysis in crisis settings, the present study employs a quantitative bibliometric methodology based on the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework. Bibliometrics is an application of mathematical and statistical tools that helps understand the intellectual structure, trajectories, and collaborations in a certain field of research. The findings outline the paradigm shifts occurring in sentiment analysis and disaster research between 2011 and 2026. This evolution has shifted the domain from early static lexicons and basic supervised classifiers to multi-modal deep learning architectures, Large Language Models (LLMs), and dynamic noise-filtering mechanisms capable of converting real-time social streams into actionable situational awareness. Increasingly, this research trajectory is propelled by urgent concerns surrounding climate-induced disasters, where social media serves as a vital digital gauge of public risk perception, panic, and community needs for emergency response planning. Technological advancements have spurred significant interest from the international community, particularly the USA and China, which currently dominate publications in this field. Given this landscape, future research is expected to foster collaboration aimed at developing AI-driven sentiment analysis capable of facilitating rapid and accurate responses. Furthermore, there is an urgent imperative for disaster-prone nations to formulate and enact policy frameworks that prioritize the deployment of systematically integrated, measurable AI-based sentiment tools within official emergency management infrastructure, bridging the gap between social data extraction and real-time operational decision-making.

Furthermore, there is an urgent imperative for disaster-prone nations to formulate and enact policy frameworks that prioritize the deployment of systematically integrated, measurable AI-based sentiment tools within official emergency management infrastructure, bridging the gap between social data extraction and real-time operational decision-making.

title: ALEX Benchmark v1.0
abstract: This dataset constitutes the frozen evaluation set for the ALEX Benchmark Protocol v1.0, a pre-registered experiment designed to test whether the ALEX cognitive architecture produces measurable improvements in analytical reasoning when the underlying large language model is held constant. The dataset contains 120 benchmark tasks distributed equally across 12 cognitive categories: Thesis Analysis, Thesis Breaking, Mispricing, Positioning & Flow, Asymmetry, Valuation, Portfolio Reasoning, Regime Dependence, Uncertainty, Adversarial Prompts, High-Stakes Reasoning, and General Reasoning. The benchmark is designed to test not only potential advantages of the ALEX architecture, but also its possible failure modes. The task set therefore includes weak-premise tests, strong-premise controls, missing-information problems, adversarial prompts, uncertainty tests, and simple controls intended to detect excessive skepticism, overconstraint, unnecessary complexity, or over-engineering. Each task has a corresponding hidden reference annotation specifying the construct being tested, intended trap or ambiguity where applicable, minimum evidence requirements, critical hidden assumptions, expected failure vectors, regime-flip conditions, and highest-value missing inputs. These evaluator annotations are intentionally withheld during the inference phase and will be released after completion of response generation, blinded scoring, and unblinding. The accompanying freeze manifest records cryptographic SHA-256 hashes of the frozen dataset files, allowing verification that the benchmark was not modified after the start of the experiment. The benchmark compares two conditions using the same underlying language model, identical task information, and equivalent generation conditions: Baseline — the underlying model without ALEX orchestration. ALEX — the same underlying model operating under the frozen ALEX cognitive architecture. Responses will be evaluated using the pre-registered ALEX Cognitive Quality Score (ACQS), a 100-point framework covering factual and logical correctness, intent alignment, assumption detection, counter-thesis quality, failure-vector identification, uncertainty calibration, expectation-gap reasoning, regime awareness, asymmetry/distribution thinking, actionability without false precision, and intellectual honesty. This dataset should be interpreted together with the pre-registered experimental protocol: Minchev, T. (2026). ALEX Benchmark Protocol v1.0: A Pre-Registered Evaluation Framework for Architecture-Induced Cognitive Performance in Large Language Models. Zenodo. Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23076424 IMPORTANT: No comparative ALEX-versus-Baseline benchmark results had been generated or inspected when Dataset v1.0 was frozen. The hidden evaluator key is deliberately excluded from the public pre-inference release and is intended for publication as part of the post-experiment reproducibility package.

title: AI Disclosure in Applied Marketing Practice: Effects of an AI Label on Advertising Credibility, Brand Authenticity, and Purchase Intention for a Sensory Experience Product
abstract: Regulatory initiatives such as the EU AI Act oblige advertisers to disclose AI-generated content, raising a transparency dilemma for applied marketing practice: an ethically required disclosure may erode consumer trust. This study examines whether an explicit AI label ("Created by AI") on an advertising image for a fictional organic natural cosmetics brand reduces advertising credibility, brand authenticity, and purchase intention, and whether individual AI literacy moderates these effects. A randomized single-factor between-subjects online experiment was conducted and analyzed in two scenarios: an intention-to-treat sample (N = 179) representing realistic exposure conditions, and a per-protocol sample (N = 125) isolating conscious label perception. No significant label effects emerged in either scenario, and brand authenticity did not mediate an effect on purchase intention. Given the limited sample size, moderate negative effects cannot be excluded, particularly for brand authenticity. More than half of the exposed participants overlooked the label entirely, indicating pronounced banner blindness in applied advertising contexts.

title: A Type System for Optimizing Dynamic IFC
abstract: Dynamic information-flow control (IFC) enforces confidentiality policies at runtime by tagging values with security labels and blocking policy-violating outputs by terminating the running system. Pervasive label tracking and enforcement checks incur high runtime costs, which limits practical IFC deployment to performance-insensitive workloads. We present a novel alternative called MinIF, a type-directed program transformation that statically eliminates the overhead of dynamic IFC for existing systems. The central contribution of MinIF is a flow-sensitive type system that tracks which sensitive inputs influence a value and whether the enforcement mechanism would accept operations on it, even though the enforced policy is unknown to the type system. Using the type system, MinIF statically predicts enforcement outcomes and removes redundant checks along with the label-tracking code that served them, and we prove that the optimized program preserves both the behavior and the enforcement decisions of the original. For IFC systems with introspection, the optimization is fully automatic, as the introspection queries already present in the program supply all the permission information MinIF needs, with no programmer annotations. Unresolved checks surface as warnings, and the absence of warnings gives developers a static guarantee against enforcement-induced system termination. We evaluate MinIF on Python programs running on the WebTTC dynamic IFC platform. On benchmarks, MinIF eliminates between 13% and 99% of the enforcement overhead, and compute-intensive workloads that time out under enforcement now complete in milliseconds.

title: How Independent U.S. Hotel Owners Decide on Guest-Facing AI, and What Follows for Staff and Guests: An Owner Survey
abstract: This study asks how owners and general managers of independent (unbranded) U.S. hotels decide whether to adopt guest-facing artificial intelligence tools (automated guest messaging, webchat and voice agents, AI-assisted check-in, AI upselling, service robots), what they have observed afterward for staff and guests, and what stops non-adopters. No prior study has asked U.S. independent hotel owners this question; the adoption models (TAM, UTAUT, UTAUT2, AIDUA) were built on employees and consumers rather than on the owner who decides, pays, employs and serves; and no study has measured staffing or guest outcomes after a hotel adopted AI. Federal policy names small-business AI adoption and worker AI literacy as priorities, sets a national visitor target the lodging sector is missing, and acknowledges that there is no national source of lodging data. The study is a cross-sectional online survey of owners (target n = 100 to 150), built from validated UTAUT2, perceived-cost, attitude and trust scales reworded to the property level, with open-text questions and an optional email or 15-minute follow-up. Seven propositions derived from the literature are tested as hypotheses. Outputs: a practitioner report for owners, an anonymized dataset deposited here, and a peer-reviewed paper. The study is conducted independently by Elena Smolenskaia.

title: Spec-Skill: A Pluggable Coding-Agent Plugin for Neuro-symbolic Program Specification Synthesis
abstract: Formal verification provides strong correctness guarantees, but its practical adoption is limited by the cost of writing precise formal specifications. While large language models can generate candidate specifications, prompt-only generation and monolithic LLM pipelines often struggle with verifier feedback, iterative repair, cross-function consistency, and project-level orchestration. Modern coding agents offer a natural interface for such tool-mediated workflows. We present Spec-Skill, a pluggable agent plugin for neuro-symbolic program specification synthesis. A host agent decomposes a C project into layered verification units and coordinates sub-agents that synthesize ACSL function contracts and loop invariants, verify them with Frama-C/WP, and repair failures using verifier feedback. A common CLI-based interface allows Spec-Skill to integrate with different coding-agent platforms, including Claude Code and Codex. We evaluate Spec-Skill on established specification-generation benchmarks and a project-scale X509-parser codebase. Spec-Skill achieves an overall Pass@5 of 98.8% across the established benchmarks and verifies 171 of 212 functions in X509-parser, demonstrating the potential of agent-oriented orchestration for project-level specification synthesis.
